sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the picker
sections.what: Loads the data tools, icons, industry and segment lists, the backdrop image and research settings used by the picker.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Renaming any imported file will stop the whole picker from loading.

sections.name: PickerScope, EMPTY_SCOPE
sections.title: Shape of a selection
sections.what: Defines what one selection holds: research settings, the peer switch, industries, segments, projects and companies, plus an empty starting value.
sections.why: Likely reason: the picker and its parent screen share one agreed shape for the selection.
sections.watch_out: A new field added here must also be handled by the parent screen and by the clear-all action.

sections.name: scopeIsEmpty, ProjectHit, CompanyHit, UnderstoodSource, Understood
sections.title: Empty check and data shapes
sections.what: Checks whether a selection is empty and describes the data returned for projects, companies and the understood-project result.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code, beyond the use of these shapes in the panels below.
sections.watch_out: These shapes are not checked at run time, so a server change will not raise a clear error here.

sections.name: sourceBadge
sections.title: Status label for a source
sections.what: Turns a source's status word into a short plain label and a colour, such as Page fetched or Access failed. Unknown words are shown with underscores replaced by spaces.
sections.why: Likely reason: the owner should read plain labels, not raw status codes.
sections.watch_out: Any new status the server sends will show as raw text until a label is added here.

sections.name: useLiveIndustries, indName, Mode
sections.title: Which industries can be chosen
sections.what: Shows only industries marked as live, plus any industry that already has projects. It also provides the short display name for an industry slug.
sections.why: The comment says empty placeholder industries stay hidden.
sections.watch_out: An industry slug that is not in the shared list displays as its raw slug.

sections.name: MODES
sections.title: The three mode tabs
sections.what: Defines the three ways to start a scope, with their icons and a short description each.
sections.why: The descriptions tell the owner what each mode does.
sections.watch_out: The order here sets the order of the tabs on screen.

sections.name: useDebounced
sections.title: Waiting for typing to pause
sections.what: Returns a copy of a text value that updates only after the user stops typing for a short time.
sections.why: Likely reason: stops a search request from being sent on every key press.
sections.watch_out: Changing the wait time changes how quickly results appear.

sections.name: ScopePicker (part 1)
sections.title: Main picker layout and selection list
sections.what: Holds the chosen mode and the labels for picked projects, and builds the list of current choices with a remove button for each. Removing an industry also removes its segments. Project labels are only known for projects added in this session, so others show a shortened id.
sections.why: The basket is the owner's running record of what the scan will cover.
sections.watch_out: A project loaded from earlier may show a shortened id instead of its name.

sections.name: ScopePicker (part 2)
sections.title: Mode tabs and active panel
sections.what: Draws the three mode buttons and the panel for the chosen mode. In project mode it adds a switch for including comparable projects, which is on unless turned off.
sections.why: The peer switch text explains that turning it off researches only the selected projects.
sections.watch_out: The peer switch is on by default unless the scope explicitly sets it to off.

sections.name: ScopePicker (part 3)
sections.title: Selection basket and start area
sections.what: The right-hand panel that lists the choices, offers clear-all, shows research options when allowed, and holds the start area supplied by the parent.
sections.why: Keeping the start control beside the list lets the owner check the selection before running.
sections.watch_out: Research options only appear when the caller allows them, so a tool that does not set this will hide them.

sections.name: Chip
sections.title: Toggle button
sections.what: A small pill-shaped button that appears selected or not and reports that state to screen readers.
sections.why: Reused for industries and segments so they look and behave the same.
sections.watch_out: The selected state is shown only through its colour and the pressed flag, so a colour-only check will miss it.

sections.name: IndustryPanel
sections.title: Industry and segment choices
sections.what: Lets the owner tick industries, and optionally narrow them to segments. Choosing a segment also adds its industry. Choosing an industry includes all its projects.
sections.why: The helper text states that selecting an industry includes every project in it.
sections.watch_out: Deselecting an industry removes all of its chosen segments at once.

sections.name: ProjectPanel (part 1)
sections.title: Project search and results
sections.what: Lets the owner type a project name, waits for a pause, searches once two characters are typed, and offers an add button for each match. Matches already chosen show as Added.
sections.why: Two-character minimum avoids very broad searches. Likely reason.
sections.watch_out: A failed search shows a retry link, but results from an earlier search can remain visible while a new one loads.

sections.name: ProjectPanel (part 2)
sections.title: Researching an unknown project
sections.what: When no Yard project matches, offers a research action that looks the project up and finds Yard peers. In replay this is replaced by a note. The result shows whether it matched the Yard, a caveat for peer-only analysis, sources with status labels, and the list of peers.
sections.why: The caveat states that no Yard record is created and no figures are estimated for a project outside the Yard.
sections.watch_out: Research is a paid live call, so pressing its button starts a charged request.

sections.name: ProjectPanel (part 3)
sections.title: Adding researched projects
sections.what: Adds the projects found by research to the selection in one step. Names come from the research reply, or a shortened id is used if no name was returned.
sections.why: Lets the owner add a whole peer group at once.
sections.watch_out: The add button is disabled when no peers were found, so an empty result cannot be added.

sections.name: CompanyPanel
sections.title: Company search and selection
sections.what: Lets the owner search company names and tick companies. Each company shows how many projects it has. A company is chosen by its name.
sections.why: The helper text says all projects of a selected company are resolved automatically.
sections.watch_out: Selecting by name means two companies with the same name would be treated as one.

summary: The screen where a user chooses what a scan covers: industries, segments, single projects or companies, shown in a running selection list with research settings and a start area.
purpose: Lets the owner build a list of projects to analyse before starting a run, and see that list as they build it.
why: Reason not stated in the code, beyond the names of the modes and the description text, which explain that a scope can be started from an industry, a project or a company.
how: 1. Shows three modes: industry, project and company. 2. Each mode has its own panel to search or pick items. 3. Every choice updates the scope passed in by the parent screen. 4. The right-hand basket lists the current choices, lets the user remove them, and shows research settings and the start area. 5. Project search and research calls go to the reality-scan API.
inputs: The current scope, a function to update it, a project search function, flags for segments, peers and research, and the start-area content.
outputs: An updated scope sent to the parent, and calls to the server for search, company lookup and project research.
risks: The project research call is paid and runs live, so it must stay off in replay. Removing an industry also removes its segments. Company selections are stored by name, not by id.
debug: If a choice does not appear in the basket, check the scope update path. If search returns nothing, check the minimum of two characters and the API response. If research does nothing, check the replay flag and the server reply.
